pool.text: Henry II, Duke of Austria, relocated the Babenberg residence to Vienna.
Vienna was officially granted city rights by the ruling authorities.
Ottoman forces advanced toward Vienna in a notable siege.
Emperor Ferdinand I created the park to use as a private hunting ground.
The Great Plague severely afflicted Vienna and killed many inhabitants.
Armenian businessman Johannes Diodato opened the first Viennese café.
The Praterstadion was opened in the Prater and later renamed.
Adolf Hitler arrived in Vienna following the entry of German troops.
The city suffered its first air raid carried out by Soviet forces.
Two anti-aircraft flak towers were built by the Nazis towering over the park.
The first democratic municipal elections were held in November.
The Austrian State Treaty came into force ending four-power control.
The international film festival known as the Viennale started hosting events.
Vienna's English Theatre was founded as the oldest in continental Europe.
Important legal documents like the Convention on the Law of Treaties were established.
The construction of the Donauinsel and excavation of the New Danube began.
The Vienna Open tennis tournament has taken place in the city.
Vienna became a United Nations headquarters city alongside other global cities.
Vienna expanded its position as a gateway following the Iron Curtain.
Vienna ranked among vegan-friendly European cities in a study by Alternative Traveler.
